item.title: Rolling-Horizon Distributionally Robust Train Scheduling Model Cuts Delays by Up to 20%
item.description:
Rolling-Horizon Distributionally Robust Train Scheduling Model Cuts Delays by Up to 20%

🔍 Overview

  • Uncertainty in resource reopening times makes train holding and rerouting decisions difficult when closures coincide with arrival delays and longer processing times.
  • A new rolling‑horizon distributionally robust model has been created to address this challenge.

🧩 How it works

  • The model updates predictions of the remaining closure duration as observations of disruption resolution become available.
  • It jointly optimizes train routes, sequences, and timings.
  • The objective is to minimize the worst‑case expected total completion delay over an ambiguity set of scenario probabilities.
  • Solution algorithm GNN‑LBBD:
    • Uses logic‑based Benders decomposition to coordinate routing and resource scheduling.
    • Constructs conditional cuts from resource‑use patterns.
    • Employs a graph neural network to decide the order in which resource‑relaxation subproblems are solved.

⚙️ Key details

  • Tested on 28 instances for a five‑track station.
  • Achieved a mean total completion delay of 61.13 train‑minutes.
  • Compared to benchmarks:
    • 16.63 % lower than tabu search.
    • 20.06 % lower than variable neighborhood search.
    • Mean computation time was close to that of tabu search.
  • Information impact (six representative instances):
    • Using observations of disruption resolution reduced mean delay by ≈21.7 %.
    • Scenario‑based and conditional‑mean predictions gave similar overall results under the same information conditions.
    • Benefits were greater in instances with alternative routes.
  • These findings suggest a link between observation use, station resource structure, and the scope for schedule adjustments.

💡 Why it matters

  • The ability to incorporate real‑time observations into a robust optimization framework enables more reliable train scheduling under uncertain disruptions.
  • The combination of Benders decomposition and graph neural networks provides a scalable approach that outperforms traditional heuristics while keeping computation times practical.
  • Understanding how resource structure influences the value of information can guide future station design and operational policies.

#trainscheduling #robustoptimization #graphneuralnetworks #bendersdecomposition

Source: Graph learning-assisted logic-based Benders decomposition for distributionally robust in-station train rescheduling under disruptions

item.title: Resistance-Curvature Guided Sampling Framework Improves Large-Scale GNN Training
item.description:
Resistance-Curvature Guided Sampling Framework Improves Large-Scale GNN Training

Subgraph sampling reduces the training cost of large‑scale graph neural networks, but existing criteria can miss the geometric roles of edges. A new resistance‑curvature‑guided sampling framework built on ERC‑LG addresses this limitation.

🔍 Overview

  • Subgraph sampling cuts training cost for large‑scale GNNs.
  • Traditional sampling may overlook geometric edge roles.
  • The proposed framework uses resistance‑curvature‑guided sampling based on ERC‑LG.

🧩 How it works

  • ERC‑LG is a curvature approximation method for large‑scale graphs.
  • It combines Johnson‑Lindenstrauss projections with regularized multi‑GPU batched conjugate gradient solvers, avoiding explicit Laplacian pseudoinverse computation and full embedding storage.
  • The resulting curvature informs node‑ and edge‑sampling probabilities for constructing GNN training subgraphs.

⚙️ Key details

  • Experiments show numerical agreement with pseudoinverse‑based curvature.
  • Runtime is reduced compared with CG‑only computation.
  • ERC‑LG‑based sampling variants achieve the highest mean accuracy on six of seven real‑world datasets in downstream node classification.
Component Purpose in ERC‑LG
Johnson‑Lindenstrauss projections Approximate curvature while avoiding full embedding storage
Regularized multi‑GPU batched conjugate gradient solvers Compute curvature without explicit Laplacian pseudoinverse

💡 Why it matters

  • Reducing training cost makes large‑scale GNNs more practical.
  • Incorporating curvature captures geometric edge roles, leading to higher classification accuracy.

#GraphNeuralNetworks #SubgraphSampling #CurvatureApproximation

Source: Scalable Subgraph Sampling via Resistance Curvature

item.title: DefaultGNN Improves Corporate Default Prediction Using Transaction Network Analysis
item.description:
DefaultGNN Improves Corporate Default Prediction Using Transaction Network Analysis

Researchers have developed DefaultGNN, a dual-perspective graph neural network framework designed to predict corporate default risk by analyzing electronic tax-invoice data.

🔍 Overview

Corporate default prediction is a critical challenge in financial risk management. Traditional models often rely on financial statements, which can be sparse or unavailable for many firms. DefaultGNN addresses this by utilizing real-world transaction histories to assess risk.

🧩 How it works

DefaultGNN operates by analyzing transaction networks from two distinct perspectives:

  • Buyer-view transaction networks
  • Seller-view transaction networks

The framework models how risk flows through these transactional relationships, revealing that risk is both role-dependent and scale-dependent. It provides interpretable network-based explanations by visualizing how distressed trading partners contribute to a firm’s default risk.

⚙️ Key details

Feature Description
Data Source Six years of real-world electronic tax-invoice data
Model Architecture Dual-perspective graph neural network
Performance Strong improvements over attribute-based and graph-based baselines
Impact Improves approval rates by 7-11%p without increasing default risk

💡 Why it matters

The system is particularly effective for firms with limited intrinsic risk signals. Validation conducted in collaboration with a licensed credit rating agency confirms that DefaultGNN’s predictions complement existing credit scoring models.

#DefaultGNN #FinTech #GraphNeuralNetworks #RiskManagement #MachineLearning

Source: DefaultGNN: A Dual-Perspective GNN Framework for Predicting Corporate Default from Buyer-Seller Transaction Networks
